# Seat B findings

## B1 [AC-1] [AC-10] — Indented code can satisfy the zero-findings status gate

Severity: HIGH
Basis: EXECUTED
Evidence strength: REPRODUCED
Trigger: A zero-findings response contains `Blocked: none` only inside an indented Markdown code block. Deployment frequency unknown. Holds everywhere; reproduced on Windows.
Evidence:
```text
plugins/pair-review/skills/pair-review/scripts/review-run.mjs:765-770
The parser skips fenced lines, then matches l.text.trim().
Four spaces or a tab therefore disappear before matching.

Command: node --input-type=module -
Called shipped run() with in-memory filesystem fixtures and shipped
validateProblems(), using phase1 --wait --native-done A,B --max-wait 1.
No filesystem writes occurred.

Fixture section:
## Checks performed
    Blocked: none

Observed:
{"name":"indented","code":0,"validated":true,"detail":["validate Phase 1: clean"]}

Controls:
healthy declaration: exit 0
declaration inside a fence: exit 1
declaration inside a quote block: exit 1
explicit blocked declaration: exit 1

Sibling inputs containing a tab or space-plus-tab also return "" from
seatBlockedLine(), meaning no block.
```
Suggested fix: Match the canonical declaration without removing code indentation; add Phase 1 regression cases for spaces and tabs.
Same shape elsewhere: `plugins/cross-review/skills/cross-review/scripts/review-run.mjs:769`; identical installed copies under both `.claude/skills/` and `.agents/skills/`, for both skills.

## B2 [AC-1] [AC-4] — Completed CLI results can leave their processes running indefinitely

Severity: HIGH
Basis: EXECUTED
Evidence strength: REPRODUCED
Trigger: A CLI emits its terminal success event and complete answer, then hangs during shutdown. The sequencer supplies timeout zero by default, so this can persist indefinitely. Frequency unknown. Reproduced on Windows.
Evidence:
```text
plugins/pair-review/skills/pair-review/scripts/review-run.mjs:411-413
return ['--timeout', String(desc.flags.timeoutS ?? 0)];

plugins/pair-review/skills/pair-review/scripts/claude-dispatch.mjs:265-278
A result event only assigns stream.result.
The promise resolves from the child's close handler.

Command: node --input-type=module -
Exposed the shipped private runner in memory. Replaced only the executable
spawn with a real Node subprocess emitting a successful result, then waiting.
No files were written.

{"stage":"success-result-received","runnerFinished":false,"processes":[{"pid":10660}]}
{"stage":"after-explicit-cleanup","processes":[],"answerRetained":"Final review answer."}

The other shared CLI runner reproduced the same issue after agent_message
and turn.completed events:

{"stage":"after-final-and-turn-completed","timeout":0,"runnerFinished":false,"processes":[{"pid":7916,"exitCode":null,"signalCode":null}]}
{"stage":"after-explicit-cleanup","runnerFinished":true,"processes":[],"answerRetained":"Final review answer."}

With timeout 1, that runner instead returned timedOut:true despite retaining
the complete answer. Normal process shutdown returned code 0.
```
Suggested fix: After a terminal success event, allow bounded shutdown grace, then stop and await the process tree while preserving the successful answer.
Same shape elsewhere: `plugins/cross-review/skills/cross-review/scripts/claude-dispatch.mjs:265`; the other shared CLI runner’s terminal-event/close handlers at lines 704/744, also reproduced. `plugins/cross-review/skills/cross-review/scripts/opencode-dispatch.mjs:599` uses the same close-only completion pattern, checked statically. Shared copies also occur in all four installed skills.

## B3 [AC-9] [AC-10] — Backtick-quoted evidence paths are still split or rewritten

Severity: LOW
Basis: EXECUTED
Evidence strength: REPRODUCED
Trigger: A quoted path contains an option-like folder component or literal percent escape. Holds everywhere; reproduced with Windows path fixtures.
Evidence:
```text
plugins/pair-review/skills/pair-review/scripts/preflight.mjs:1425-1429
decodeFileUrls(word) runs on every path.
The option regex rejects the quoted item before stat() checks the whole path.

plugins/pair-review/skills/pair-review/scripts/path-utils.mjs:30-32
Percent escapes are decoded across the entire supplied string.

Command: node --input-type=module -
Called shipped packetReach() with a read-only stat fixture exposing exactly
three existing files. Each input was wrapped in backticks.

Input: C:\review-fixture\release -final\evidence.log
Result: outside=[], notFound=[]

Input: C:\review-fixture\percent%20literal\evidence.log
Result: outside=[]
        notFound=["C:\review-fixture\percent literal\evidence.log"]

Control: C:\review-fixture\plain space\evidence.log
Result: outside=["C:\review-fixture\plain space\evidence.log"]

The previous quoted-path branch checked the whole existing path first.
The new branch loses both existing paths.
```
Suggested fix: Check the complete literal quoted path before command classification, and decode percent escapes only within file URLs.
Same shape elsewhere: `plugins/cross-review/skills/cross-review/scripts/preflight.mjs:1425` and `scripts/path-utils.mjs:30`; identical installed copies. Both preflight reach probing and Phase 1 path warnings consume this scanner.

## B4 [AC-5] [AC-10] — Valid single-digit endpoint ports are silently omitted

Severity: LOW
Basis: EXECUTED
Evidence strength: REPRODUCED
Trigger: A packet names a valid endpoint using port 1–9. Only the advisory reach probe is affected. Holds everywhere.
Evidence:
```text
plugins/pair-review/skills/pair-review/scripts/preflight.mjs:1504-1506
Both endpoint expressions require (\d{2,5}).

Command: node --input-type=module -
Called shipped packetPorts().

Input:
tcp://localhost:7/ http://localhost:8/ localhost:9 127.0.0.1:6 [::1]:5
Output:
[]

Sibling control:
tcp://localhost:17/ http://localhost:18/ localhost:19 127.0.0.1:16 [::1]:15
Output:
["localhost:17","localhost:18","localhost:19","127.0.0.1:16","[::1]:15"]
```
Suggested fix: Accept one through five port digits in both expressions.
Same shape elsewhere: `plugins/cross-review/skills/cross-review/scripts/preflight.mjs:1504-1506`; identical installed copies. Both URL and bare-address branches have the restriction.

## B5 [AC-5] — Cross-review’s entry page incorrectly restricts the second reviewer to a CLI

Severity: MEDIUM
Basis: EXECUTED
Evidence strength: REPRODUCED
Trigger: A user follows the entry page’s CLI-only restriction on the alternate host. The default supported trial configuration instead requires a native second reviewer. Holds everywhere.
Evidence:
```text
plugins/cross-review/skills/cross-review/SKILL.md:21-24
The entry paragraph restricts the second reviewer to CLI/bridge execution,
says no other layout has a defined dispatch path, and says configuration
enforces that restriction.

plugins/cross-review/skills/cross-review/scripts/review-config.mjs:189
transport: seat.runtime === nativeRuntime ? (transport ?? 'native') : 'cli'

Command: node --input-type=module -
Called shipped buildSeats(), evaluateSupport() and validateSupport().
Used a successful-session-probe support fixture; no live probe was run.

{"transport":null,"secondTransport":"native","statuses":["probe","trial","trial"],"accepted":true}
{"transport":"cli","secondTransport":"cli","statuses":["probe","unsupported","trial"],"accepted":false}

The host reference separately documents the native second-reviewer route.
```
Suggested fix: Qualify the entry paragraph by host and explicitly allow the native route described in the host reference.
Same shape elsewhere: none found in the other entry page, README, or host tables searched.

## Checks performed

- AC-2: Checked packet/rules guards, identity-path masking, audit retry sanitization, and grant checks. Paid actor round trips were outside this read-only review. PARTIAL

Accepted deviations retained. Full suites and historical reproductions were not rerun because they write files. PARTIAL
- AC-9: Whole quoted paths previously accepted are now split or decoded incorrectly (B3). Removed wording guesses and bare-host probing match declared changes; other examined narrowing produced no additional regression. NOT MET
- AC-10: Status and path tests omit reproduced broken sibling inputs; endpoint tests omit single-digit ports (B1, B3, B4). Author-reported mutation results were not treated as executed evidence. NOT MET
- H1: Standalone malformed, fenced, and quoted declarations stop. Indented code passes; conflicting duplicates, earlier declarations, and malformed trailing declarations also pass the exercised gate. PARTLY CONFIRMED
- H2: CRLF, trailing spaces, and `None.` work. Bold labels are deliberately outside the required format. REFUTED
- H3: Terminal answers remain pending until process exit; bounded runs become timeout failures. Answers remain in result data, and the sequencer default is unlimited rather than 1800 seconds. PARTLY CONFIRMED
- H4: No additional persistent leak after process exit was demonstrated. Owned-process lists were empty after awaited cleanup. Full dispatcher/job interruption tests were not run because they write files; system-wide listing was denied. REFUTED
- H5: Static traces cover concurrent cache publication, spaced/non-ASCII paths, corrupt assemblies, and version-derived cache names. Failures reach the fallback before command execution. DLL-writing race tests were not executable within this review’s no-write constraint. REFUTED
- H6: Exercised quoted paths, line/column suffixes, brackets, rootless paths, file URLs, and command suffixes. Those controls pass; option-like components and literal percent escapes fail (B3). PARTLY CONFIRMED
- H7: Executed absolute, Git Bash, relative, home-relative, file-URL, rootless, and parent-segment guard cases; all refused. Sibling control passed. Junction handling was traced through native realpath; POSIX variable expansion was exercised with explicit platform arguments. REFUTED
- H8: Found the entry-page transport contradiction (B5). No project/vendor-domain coupling found in the searched protocol and brief text. CONFIRMED
- Repository validation passed. All four installed copies matched repository bytes: 100 files per pair-review copy, 104 per cross-review copy.
- Six syntax checks passed. Full test suites were intentionally not run because no scratch folder or filesystem writes were authorized.
- Coverage: read fully — closing diff hunks, four feedback files, smaller core helpers and benchmark helpers; read partly — large lifecycle, dispatch, translation, reporting, documentation, and test files; not read — remaining unchanged tests and fixtures.
